sentences.en: So the way that they would do this is they will hit you with tax bills, they will hit you with fines, they will intimidate you, they will
sentences.zh: 他们这样做的方式是，他们会向你开出巨额税单，他们会对你罚款，他们会恐吓你，他们会

sentences.en: basically put every possible bit of pressure on you to give up your business.
sentences.zh: 基本上对你施加一切可能的压力，迫使你放弃你的生意。

sentences.en: To sell up and get out.
sentences.zh: 低价变卖并滚蛋。

sentences.en: To get out.
sentences.zh: 滚出这里。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And the people who collaborate in this, the people who gain from it are all the big names of the German economy.
sentences.zh: 而参与其中、从中获利的人，都是德国经济界的大人物。

sentences.en: So anyone who follows football will know that Bayern Munich Stadium is called the Allianz Arena, the stadium in Munich.
sentences.zh: 所以任何关注足球的人都会知道拜仁慕尼黑的体育场叫安联球场，也就是慕尼黑的那个体育场。

sentences.en: Allianz is one of the companies that benefits from this, that takes over Jewish businesses.
sentences.zh: 安联就是从中受益、接管犹太企业公司的其中之一。

sentences.en: But Allianz are not alone.
sentences.zh: 但安联并不是唯一的一个。

sentences.en: I'm not singling them out of some prejudice or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我并不是出于某种偏见而专门挑出他们。

sentences.en: Krupp, Tyson, Flick, IG Farben, the Deutsche Bank, the Dresdner Bank.
sentences.zh: 克虏伯、蒂森、弗里克、法本公司、德意志银行、德累斯顿银行。

sentences.en: These are the big names of German economic life.
sentences.zh: 这些都是德国经济界的大腕。

sentences.en: And they all gain from taking over their Jewish rivals, taking over Jewish property, premises, you know, hoovering up bits of their markets, all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们都通过接管犹太竞争对手、接管犹太人的财产、房产、蚕食对方的市场份额等各种方式从中获利。

sentences.en: And presumably leading Nazis as well are benefiting.
sentences.zh: 想必纳粹高层也从中获益了。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So we've talked about how Göring loves a bit of plunder.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论过戈培尔如何热衷于掠夺。

sentences.en: A fur coat.
sentences.zh: 一件皮草大衣。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Nazis are prospering.
sentences.zh: 纳粹发迹了。

sentences.en: But you don't have to be a Nazi to do it.
sentences.zh: 但你不需要成为一个纳粹分子也能干这事。

sentences.en: But you remember the episode that we did on Unity Mitford, where Hitler gives her a flat and she goes around Munich and she has a choice of three flats.
sentences.zh: 还记得我们做过关于尤妮蒂·米特福德的那期节目吗？希特勒送了她一套公寓，她走遍慕尼黑，有三套公寓可供选择。

sentences.en: And she ends up in one of them and says, oh, I'll have this and goes around saying, oh, we'll get rid of these curtains.
sentences.zh: 她最后住进了其中一套，说，哦，我要这套，然后四处转悠着说，哦，我们要把这些窗帘扔掉。

sentences.en: We'll have new chairs here.
sentences.zh: 我们要在这里换上新椅子。

sentences.en: While the former owners of the flat are sobbing in the hall, surrounded by the few fragments that they've been allowed.
sentences.zh: 当公寓的前房主们在门厅里啜泣时，周围只有他们仅存的一点被允许带走的零星家当。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a terrible process.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个可怕的过程。

sentences.en: But you could see that, Tom, as a metaphor for what happens generally in the German economy.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，你可以把这看作是德国经济中普遍发生的事情的一个隐喻。

sentences.en: So the people who benefit from basically the expulsion of the Jews from the mainstream of
sentences.zh: 所以那些基本上受益于犹太人被驱逐出主流

sentences.en: German life, they're not just Göring and other corrupt Nazi functionaries.
sentences.zh: 德国生活的人，不仅仅是戈林和其他腐败的纳粹官员。

sentences.en: They are doctors and lawyers, people who think, brilliant, my Jewish competitors are out of the way.
sentences.zh: 他们是医生和律师，那些心想“太棒了，我的犹太竞争对手出局了”的人。

sentences.en: I can take their customers.
sentences.zh: 我可以抢他们的客户。

sentences.en: All good for me.
sentences.zh: 对我全都有利。

sentences.en: You know, university professors and academics start tailoring their research to the demands of the demands of the Nazi regime.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大学教授和学者开始根据纳粹政权的要求来调整他们的研究方向。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you're an academic, you might turn your hand to studies showing how you can measure a Jewish skull or a history showing
sentences.zh: 因此，举个例子，如果你是一个学者，你可能会着手研究如何测量犹太人的头骨，或者撰写历史来证明

sentences.en: how the Jews have have always betrayed Germany or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 犹太人是如何一贯背叛德国的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Think of Carl Schmitt, the jurist, yeah, who even well before this had been proposing that any book by any Jewish scholar should be put into its own category.
sentences.zh: 想想法学家卡尔·施密特，是的，甚至在此之前很久，他就提议将任何犹太学者的书都归入一个单独的类别。

sentences.en: There should be a kind of Jewish section in every library, you know, quarantined.
sentences.zh: 每个图书馆里都应该有一种犹太专区，你知道的，被隔离起来。

sentences.en: So it's not as though this is being forced on
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是说这是强加给

sentences.en: German academics.
sentences.zh: 德国学者的。

sentences.en: I mean, they are enthusiastic collaborators in it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们是其中狂热的合作者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think by 1938, by the summer of 1938, so many different branches of kind of civil
sentences.zh: 我想到了1938年，到1938年夏天，公民社会的许多不同分支

sentences.en: society, judges, lawyers, policemen, just people who run things or indeed, you know, shopkeepers who've seen their rivals eliminated.
sentences.zh: 法官、律师、警察，或者只是那些经营事务的人，甚至是那些看到竞争对手被消灭的店主。

sentences.en: All of these people are complicit now.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人现在都是同谋了。

sentences.en: They're in on it.
sentences.zh: 他们都深陷其中。

sentences.en: Once you are in on it, there's no going back, as it were, because you don't want to admit that you were wrong or that the process was wrong to begin with.
sentences.zh: 一旦你卷进去了，可以说就再也无法回头了，因为你不想承认自己错了，或者这个过程一开始就错了。

sentences.en: So that ratcheting up has really had an effect on lots of different areas of society.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种不断升级确实对社会的许多不同领域产生了影响。

sentences.en: And it's been directed from the Fuhrer.
sentences.zh: 这是由元首直接指挥的。

sentences.en: He has set the tone, but then people on the ground have kind of responded to it.
sentences.zh: 他定下了基调，然后底层的人们对此做出了某种回应。

sentences.en: So it's not just this is a top-down totalitarian system.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是一个自上而下的极权主义系统。

sentences.en: That's not how the Nazi dictatorship works.
sentences.zh: 纳粹独裁政权不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: No, because, I mean, this is the whole point of Hitler comparing himself to Pericles, who is famous as the great democratic leader of Athens.
sentences.zh: 不，因为，我的意思是，这就是希特勒把自己比作伯里克利的核心意义，伯里克利作为雅典伟大的民主领袖而闻名。

sentences.en: But Pericles is the embodiment of the will to power, as the Nazis see it.
sentences.zh: 但在纳粹看来，伯里克利是权力意志的化身。

sentences.en: And Hitler is the same, that what is happening is cast as an expression of a primordial racial impulse.
sentences.zh: 希特勒也是如此，正在发生的事情被描绘成一种原始种族冲动的表达。

sentences.en: And that Hitler is merely the standard bearer for this.
sentences.zh: 而希特勒仅仅是这一冲动的旗手。

sentences.en: And that the German people are being awakened to this racial heritage.
sentences.zh: 德国人民正在被唤醒，去认识这种种族遗产。

sentences.en: And this explains what is now happening.
sentences.zh: 这就解释了现在正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: It's a measure of the Nazi achievement that they have encouraged this.
sentences.zh: 他们鼓励了这种行为，这是纳粹成就的一个体现。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now that violence is always still there.
sentences.zh: 现在那种暴力仍然一直存在。

sentences.en: And it's actually got worse in the summer of 1938.
sentences.zh: 而且在1938年夏天实际上变得更糟了。

sentences.en: So there are attacks on Jewish homes.
sentences.zh: 所以出现了针对犹太人住所的袭击。

sentences.en: There are attacks on the remaining doctor surgeries or law firms or shops or whatever.
sentences.zh: 出现了针对仅存的犹太人诊所、律师事务所、商店或诸如此类的袭击。

sentences.en: And that really reaches a peak in about June or July 1938.
sentences.zh: 这在1938年6月或7月左右真正达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: So there's a real, what Richard Evans describes as a pogrom-like atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 因此，理查德·埃文斯所描述的那种大屠杀般的氛围真实存在。

sentences.en: There's a sense that something is brewing.
sentences.zh: 有一种风雨欲来的感觉。

sentences.en: Of course, the question is, you know, all this business that they've been saying, this rhetorical
sentences.zh: 当然，问题是，你知道，所有这些他们一直在说的言论，关于

sentences.en: stuff about removing Jews from Germany or indeed from Europe, how are they going to do that?
sentences.zh: 将犹太人从德国甚至从欧洲清除的豪言壮语，他们到底要怎么做？

sentences.en: You know, will intimidating people into fleeing the Reich be enough?
sentences.zh: 你知道，仅仅通过恐吓让人民逃离德意志帝国就足够了吗？

sentences.en: And at this point, they are contemplating lots of different schemes.
sentences.zh: 在这个时候，他们正在考虑各种不同的方案。

sentences.en: So one of them, very famously, is about reaching some sort of deal with a foreign country, a foreign land, which will take the entire Jewish population of Germany.
sentences.zh: 其中一个非常著名的方案是与一个能够接纳德国全部犹太人口的外国或境外领土达成某种协议。

sentences.en: So not Rwanda, but Madagascar.
sentences.zh: 所以不是卢旺达，而是马达加斯加。

sentences.en: Madagascar.
sentences.zh: 马达加斯加。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没得错。

sentences.en: So Goebbels makes a note, the Führer wants to push them all out, negotiate with Poland and Romania.
sentences.zh: 因此，戈培尔记录道，元首想要把他们全部赶出去，与波兰和罗马尼亚进行谈判。

sentences.en: Madagascar would be most suitable.
sentences.zh: 马达加斯加将是最合适的。

sentences.en: So this is an idea that runs right through the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个贯穿整个20世纪30年代的想法。

sentences.en: It's incredibly sort of implausible.
sentences.zh: 这简直难以置信。

sentences.en: It's a fanciful idea, but that's one notion.
sentences.zh: 这是一个异想天开的想法，但确实是其中一个方案。

sentences.en: Palestine, which we mentioned last time, is another idea.
sentences.zh: 我们上次提到过的巴勒斯坦是另一个想法。

sentences.en: So there's a guy called Leopold von Mildenstein, who's an SS man.
sentences.zh: 有个叫利奥波德·冯·米尔登斯坦的家伙，他是一个党卫队队员。

sentences.en: He goes to Palestine and he has meetings with
sentences.zh: 他去了巴勒斯坦，并与

sentences.en: Zionists.
sentences.zh: 犹太复国主义者会面。

sentences.en: He's the guy who was Eichmann's boss, kind of leading that whole drive.
sentences.zh: 他就是艾希曼的上司，某种程度上领导了整个行动。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes, he was.
sentences.zh: 是的，他就是。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He was.
sentences.zh: 他就是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But actually a lot of Nazis don't quite like that idea because they think if we establish a
sentences.zh: 但实际上许多纳粹分子并不太喜欢这个想法，因为他们认为如果我们

sentences.en: Jewish homeland in Palestine, well, we're just storing up trouble for ourselves later on.
sentences.zh: 在巴勒斯坦建立一个犹太人家园，那么我们只是在为自己日后埋下祸根。

sentences.en: Potential threat.
sentences.zh: 潜在的威胁。

sentences.en: I mean, one day that will be the base for an enemy empire that will want to fight us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，总有一天那里会成为一个敌对帝国的基地，想要与我们对抗。

sentences.en: So obviously that's not a good idea.
sentences.zh: 所以这显然不是个好主意。

sentences.en: Now there's another idea, which is we just basically find some kind of barren wasteland.
sentences.zh: 现在还有另一个想法，那就是我们基本上找个什么不毛之地。

sentences.en: You know, who knows?
sentences.zh: 你知道，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Maybe when we've conquered the Soviet
sentences.zh: 也许当我们征服了苏联

sentences.en: Union, we put them all in Siberia or whatever.
sentences.zh: 之后，就把他们全扔到西伯利亚或者什么地方去。

sentences.en: Because that's the theme of Michael Chabon's great novel, The Yiddish Policeman's Union, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为那是迈克尔·夏邦的伟大小说《犹太警察工会》的主题，不是吗？

sentences.en: Where they all end up in Canada.
sentences.zh: 小说里他们最后都去了加拿大。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's kind of alternative history where Jews haven't gone to Palestine.
sentences.zh: 这是一种替代历史，犹太人没有去巴勒斯坦。

sentences.en: They've gone to the frozen wastes of the American North.
sentences.zh: 他们去了美洲北部冰冻的荒原。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think that idea about the frozen waste is really important because it reminds us this is always latently genocidal.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于冰冻荒原的那个想法真的很重要，因为它提醒我们这始终带有潜在的灭绝人性色彩。

sentences.en: The idea is not, let's find them a place to live where they can just crack on and, you know, we can forget about them.
sentences.zh: 这个想法不是说，让我们为他们找个可以安居乐业、自力更生的敌方，然后我们可以忘掉他们。

sentences.en: It is, let us find a place to put them where they will die.
sentences.zh: 而是，让我们把他们放在一个会让他们死去的地方。

sentences.en: And that is why one thing that we haven't mentioned, but which of course certainly people in Britain will know, is that it's very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有一件事我们没有提到，但英国人肯定知道的，那就是这非常困难。

sentences.en: I mean, the reason that the Nazis are having all these arguments is because Jews cannot emigrate easily to countries like Britain, to
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，纳粹之所以有这么多争论，是因为犹太人无法轻易移民到英国、

sentences.en: France, to America, because there are limits put up there.
sentences.zh: 法国、美国这样的国家，因为那里设置了限制。

sentences.en: But also presumably they don't want to let them go to prosperous and successful economies because there the threat will be even more paramount.
sentences.zh: 但据推测，他们也不想让他们去繁荣成功的经济体，因为那里的威胁会更加突出。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, don't forget, they're saying again and again, they must be removed from Europe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，别忘了，他们一遍又一遍地说，必须把他们从欧洲清除出去。

sentences.en: Goebbels says that.
sentences.zh: 戈培尔就是这么说的。

sentences.en: So in other words, if they all go to live in the Netherlands or in France or in London, that is sub-ideal from the Nazi point of view because the terrible
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果他们都去荷兰、法国或伦敦生活，从纳粹的角度来看这并不理想，因为那种可怕的

sentences.en: apocalyptic threat is still there.
sentences.zh: 末日威胁依然存在。

sentences.en: People have these great arguments about where the Holocaust originated, when was the order given for the final solution or this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 人们对于大屠杀起源于何处、最终解决方案的命令是什么时候下达的之类的问题有过很多激烈的争论。

sentences.en: To my mind, there is clearly a genocidal impulse, if only rhetorically there all through the
sentences.zh: 在我看来，整个20世纪30年代，即使只是在口头上，也明显存在一种种族灭绝的冲动

sentences.en: 1930s and it has become more and more pronounced.
sentences.zh: 并且这种冲动变得越来越明显。

sentences.en: I mean, we introduced the previous episode with Hitler talking about rotting corpses of
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在上一集开头时提到过希特勒谈到

sentences.en: Jews hanging from the gallows in Munich.
sentences.zh: 挂在慕尼黑绞刑架上的犹太人腐烂尸体。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, it's been there from the beginning, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从一开始就有了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely it has.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样的。

sentences.en: So let me just end this half of the episode with an example of how this might affect one particular Jewish family.
sentences.zh: 那么让我用一个例子来结束本集的上半部分，看看这会如何影响某个特定的犹太家庭。

sentences.en: We'll pick a family called the Grinchbands.
sentences.zh: 我们挑一个叫格林奇班德的家庭。

sentences.en: So they are Jews originally from Poland.
sentences.zh: 所以他们原本是来自波兰的犹太人。

sentences.en: They had come to Germany in 1911 and settled in
sentences.zh: 他们在1911年来到德国，并在汉诺威定居

sentences.en: Hanover and opened a tailor shop, Zindel and Rivka Grinchband.
sentences.zh: 开了一家裁缝店，辛德尔和里夫卡·格林奇班德。

sentences.en: They are Yiddish speaking, what are called Ostjuden, so Jews from the EaSt. And they have a son born in 1921 called
sentences.zh: 他们说意第绪语，被称为“东欧犹太人”，也就是来自东欧的犹太人。他们有一个1921年出生的儿子叫

sentences.en: Herschel.
sentences.zh: 赫舍尔。

sentences.en: He's a bright boy, but very sensitive.
sentences.zh: 他是一个聪明的男孩，但非常敏感。

sentences.en: He feels his Jewishness very keenly.
sentences.zh: 他对自己犹太人身份的感受极其敏锐。

sentences.en: He's bullied at school because he's Jewish.
sentences.zh: 他在学校里因为自己是犹太人而被欺负。

sentences.en: He wants to emigrate to Palestine.
sentences.zh: 他想移民到巴勒斯坦。

sentences.en: So he does want to join the Zionists, but he's told he's too young.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实想加入犹太复国主义者，但被告知他太年轻了。

sentences.en: So he's sent off to live with an uncle and aunt in Paris.
sentences.zh: 于是他被送往巴黎和他的叔叔阿姨一起生活。

sentences.en: So from the Nazi perspective, they're pleased he's gone, but this is a sub-ideal solution.
sentences.zh: 所以从纳粹的角度来看，他们很高兴他走了，但这并不是一个理想的解决方案。

sentences.en: In Paris, he lives with other sort of Polish Orthodox Jews.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎，他和一些其他的波兰正统犹太人生活在一起。

sentences.en: He doesn't really mix much.
sentences.zh: 他其实不怎么与外界交往。

sentences.en: He doesn't learn French.
sentences.zh: 他没有学法语。

sentences.en: He speaks Yiddish.
sentences.zh: 他说意第绪语。

sentences.en: And he reads at the end of 1938 that in Poland, the authorities there responding to anti-Semitic pressure want to strip Polish Jews living abroad of their Polish citizenship.
sentences.zh: 他在1938年底读到消息称，在波兰，当地当局为了回应反犹太主义压力，想要剥夺旅居国外的波兰犹太人的波兰公民身份。

sentences.en: And in response, so this is interesting, it's the Nazis responding to another Central European state.
sentences.zh: 作为回应，所以这很有意思，这是纳粹对另一个中欧国家的回应。

sentences.zh: 他们强迫他的家人下到地窖里。

sentences.en: Then they force the family to smash all their own wine bottles in the cellar and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 然后强迫全家人砸碎地窖里他们自己的所有酒瓶以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And then at the end,
sentences.zh: 最后，

sentences.en: Meyer himself, they try to get out to the railway station.
sentences.zh: 迈尔自己试图逃到火车站去。

sentences.en: He ends up being arrested.
sentences.zh: 结果他还是被捕了。

sentences.en: And this sort of scene is repeated in towns all across Germany.
sentences.zh: 德国各地的城镇都在重复着这样的场景。

sentences.en: The other example I was going to pick from Richard Evans' book, it's just a tiny thing, but it's really heartbreaking.
sentences.zh: 我本来打算从理查德·埃文斯的书里选的另一个例子，虽然只是一件小事，但真的非常让人心碎。

sentences.en: In a place called Esslingen in Baden-Württemberg, which is near Stuttgart, there was a Jewish orphanage.
sentences.zh: 在巴登-符腾堡州一个叫埃斯林根的地方，靠近斯图加特，那里有一所犹太孤儿院。

sentences.en: And people break into the orphanage with axes and sledgehammers.
sentences.zh: 人们拿着斧头和大锤闯入孤儿院。

sentences.en: They destroy everything, the kids' books or their religious stuff, anything they can find, toys.
sentences.zh: 他们摧毁了一切，孩子们的书、宗教物品、任何他们能找到的东西、玩具。

sentences.en: Yeah, they burn them all.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们把这些全烧了。

sentences.en: And then they say to the children,
sentences.zh: 然后他们对孩子们说，

sentences.en: if you do not leave, we will burn you too.
sentences.zh: 如果你们不离开，我们连你们一块烧死。

sentences.en: So you have these poor kids straggling along the roads in the dark, walking for hours in tears, and they have to basically walk all the way to Stuttgart,
sentences.zh: 于是这些可怜的孩子们在黑暗中艰难地沿路前行，泪流满面地走了好几个小时，他们基本上得一路步行到斯图加特，

sentences.en: which I think is about three hours away, before they can find anyone to shelter them or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我想大概要走三个小时左右，才能找到能收留他们或者提供类似庇护的地方。

sentences.en: I mean, that's just one scene among thousands upon thousands.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是成千上万个场景中的一个。

sentences.en: As all the reports of this flood in, Goebbels and Hitler are delighted.
sentences.zh: 随着所有这些报告如潮水般涌来，戈培尔和希特勒高兴极了。

sentences.en: I mean, Goebbels writes in his diary, the people's anger is raging.
sentences.zh: 我是说，戈培尔在他的日记中写道，人民的愤怒正在怒吼。

sentences.en: Nothing can be done against it.
sentences.zh: 对此无可奈何。

sentences.en: And I don't want to do anything either.
sentences.zh: 我也不想做任何干预。

sentences.en: It should be given free reign.
sentences.zh: 就应该让它自由发展。

sentences.en: As I drive back to my hotel, the windows shatter.
sentences.zh: 当我开车返回酒店时，窗户都被砸碎了。

sentences.en: Bravo, bravo.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，太棒了。

sentences.en: The synagogues are burning in all the big cities.
sentences.zh: 各大城市的犹太教堂都在燃烧。

sentences.en: You know, the delight, the glee.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种狂喜，那种幸灾乐祸。

sentences.en: You talked before about the kind of, the way that the Nazis rationalize and they intellectualize what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 你之前谈到过纳粹对他们所作所为的那种合理化和知识分子式的包装。

sentences.en: But there is a kind of savagery.
sentences.zh: 但其中本质上还是一种野蛮行径。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: A relish.
sentences.zh: 一种幸灾乐祸。

sentences.en: You know, that sadistic joy and destruction, which we shouldn't lose sight of.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种虐待狂式的快乐和破坏欲，我们不应忽视这一点。

sentences.en: But Dominic, this whole thing has been set up as being a spontaneous expression of public will.
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，整件事一直被包装成公众意志的自发表达。

sentences.en: So what is the kind of official position of the Nazi hierarchy and what's happening?
sentences.zh: 那么纳粹高层的官方立场是什么？现在情况如何？

sentences.en: They absolutely back it.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对给予支持。

sentences.en: They say it's a completely reasonable expression of the utterly justifiable anger of the German people who have been victimized and brutalized by a worldwide jury for too long.
sentences.zh: 他们声称，这是德国人民完全合情合理的诉求，表达了他们因长期遭到世界陪审团的迫害和虐待而产生的、完全正当的愤怒。

sentences.en: However,
sentences.zh: 然而，

sentences.en: you know, they don't want the disorder to get completely out of control.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们也不希望混乱彻底失控。

sentences.en: So the following lunchtime, Goebbels goes to the Osteria in Munich, which of course is Hitler's favorite restaurant.
sentences.zh: 因此在接下来的午餐时间，戈培尔前往慕尼黑的“奥斯特里亚”餐厅，这当然是希特勒最喜欢的餐厅。

sentences.en: It's the restaurant, Tom, I'll mention it before you do, that Unity Mitford used to hang out at in a hope of catching Hitler's eye.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这家餐厅——我抢在你之前说出来——尤妮蒂·米特福德过去常在那里闲逛，希望能吸引希特勒的注意。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There, Hitler issues an order, you know, end of the action, stop.
sentences.zh: 在那里，希特勒下达了一道命令，你知道的，行动结束，停手。

sentences.en: And of course, the terrible thing is that, I mean, it's one of many terrible things, is it doesn't stop, that it actually
sentences.zh: 当然，最可怕的事情在于——我的意思是，这是诸多可怕事情之一——它并没有停止，实际上它

sentences.en: continues, that now so many people have a taste for the sadism and the cruelty.
sentences.zh: 仍在继续，因为现在有太多人迷恋上了虐待狂行径和残暴行为。

sentences.en: So again, the examples of the next couple of days, Jews are forced to sing religious songs in the street,
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来几天里，类似的事情再次发生：犹太人被迫在街头唱宗教歌曲，

sentences.en: they're drenched in water, they're kicked and they're made to dance outside the synagogue.
sentences.zh: 他们被泼水、遭到踢打，还被迫在犹太教堂外跳舞。

sentences.en: In Essen, Jewish men are rounded up and their beards are set on fire.
sentences.zh: 在埃森，犹太男子被集中起来，他们的胡须被点燃。

sentences.en: In a place called Mepen, they're made to lie down outside the Stormtrooper headquarters, the SA headquarters, and then the brown shirts literally walk over the top of them.
sentences.zh: 在一个叫梅彭的地方，他们被迫趴在冲锋队总部——SA总部——外面，然后那些穿棕衫的人直接从他们身上踩过去。

sentences.en: The really shocking thing actually is, and we've mentioned this so many times in this series, I still find it, you know, it's sort of
sentences.zh: 真正令人震惊的其实是——我们在本系列节目中已经多次提到这一点，我仍然觉得，你知道，这有点

sentences.en: haunting and terrifying how much children and young people are involved in these events.
sentences.zh: 挥之不去且令人毛骨悚然，儿童和年轻人竟然如此深度地参与到这些事件中。

sentences.en: So in Frankfurt, for example, kids are taken out of school to spit at the Jews who have been rounded up.
sentences.zh: 所以在法兰克福，举个例子，孩子们被带出学校，去向被集中的犹太人吐口水。

sentences.en: But it's not surprising, is it?
sentences.zh: 但这并不令人意外，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, if they've been indoctrinated in this, that's what they're going to do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果他们被灌输了这些思想，他们自然就会这么做。

sentences.en: No, I guess it's not surprising, Tom.
sentences.zh: 不，我想这并不意外，汤姆。

sentences.en: No, it's not surprising at all.
sentences.zh: 不，一点也不意外。

sentences.en: The morality they've been taught is a Nazi morality.
sentences.zh: 他们被教导的道德是一种纳粹道德。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Where what they're doing is the right thing.
sentences.zh: 在那种道德里，他们所做的是正确的事。

sentences.en: It's a good thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件好事。

sentences.en: It's moral.
sentences.zh: 这是有道德的。

sentences.en: It's for the good of the race.
sentences.zh: 这是为了种族的利益。

sentences.en: But it's nonetheless horrifying there, right?
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，这依然令人毛骨悚然，对吧？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, in the Tsar land, there are stories about Jewish people trying to escape and mobs of small children running after them, kicking them, throwing stones at them,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在萨尔地区，有报道称犹太人试图逃跑，成群的小孩子在后面追赶他们、踢他们、向他们扔石头、

sentences.en: hitting them with sticks, you know, making them fall to the ground and then hitting them and all this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 用棍子打他们，你知道的，让他们摔倒在地，然后殴打他们，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of diabolical.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是丧心病狂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So enormous amounts of damage, you know, hundreds of millions of marks worth of damage when they finally clear up all the broken glass.
sentences.zh: 因此造成了巨大的破坏，当他们最终清理完所有的碎玻璃时，损失高达数亿马克。

sentences.en: And that's where the name Kristallnacht comes from.
sentences.zh: 这就是“水晶之夜”这个名字的由来。

sentences.en: The Reichskristallnacht, yeah.
sentences.zh: 帝国水晶之夜，对。

sentences.en: The Knights of Broken Glass.
sentences.zh: 碎玻璃之夜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: How many people died?
sentences.zh: 有多少人死亡？

sentences.en: Some estimates as low as a couple of hundred, some into the early thousands, kind of one, two, three thousand.
sentences.zh: 有些估计仅两百人左右，有些则达到了一两千人，大概在一千到三千人之间。

sentences.en: As in Vienna, we talked about this in the
sentences.zh: 正如在维也纳那样，我们在

sentences.en: Anschluss episode.
sentences.zh: 德奥合并那一集里谈过。

sentences.en: Some people kill themselves.
sentences.zh: 有些人自杀了。

sentences.en: About 30,000 people ended up being arrested and imprisoned in concentration camps.
sentences.zh: 大约有3万人最终被捕并关押进集中营。

sentences.en: Are there rapes?
sentences.zh: 有发生强暴吗？

sentences.en: Do you know, I don't know, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我不知道，汤姆。

sentences.en: Because that would be illegal, presumably.
sentences.zh: 因为据推测那应该是违法的。

sentences.en: It would be against the law?
sentences.zh: 那将是违法的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Is there any hint of sexual violence?
sentences.zh: 有任何性暴力的迹象吗？

sentences.en: I haven't seen any in the history books that I've read.
sentences.zh: 在我读过的历史书中没有看到过。

sentences.en: So probably not.
sentences.zh: 所以可能没有。

sentences.en: Perhaps not.
sentences.zh: 也许没有。

sentences.en: Perhaps the taboo is so great.
sentences.zh: 也许这个禁忌太大了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But no, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 但总之，我想没有。

sentences.en: But in general, I think there's a sense that this is an absolute watershed.
sentences.zh: 不过总体而言，我认为人们有一种感觉，即这是一个绝对的分水岭。

sentences.en: It is clear now beyond the slightest shadow of a doubt that there is nothing that the Nazis are not prepared to do to the Jews.
sentences.zh: 现在毫无疑问地清楚了，纳粹对犹太人可以说是无所不用其极。

sentences.en: And whatever they do do, nobody will try to stop them.
sentences.zh: 无论他们做什么，都不会有人试图阻止他们。

sentences.en: Well, except Dominic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，除了多米尼克你。

sentences.en: There is still a shadow of a doubt, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 仍然有一丝疑虑，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, no one at this stage, even now, is thinking that there might be industrialized extermination of Jews.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，在这个阶段，甚至到现在，没有人会想到可能会对犹太人进行工业化的灭绝。

sentences.en: That's fair.
sentences.zh: 这倒也是。

sentences.en: But it's plausible that they will organize pogrom after pogrom.
sentences.zh: 但他们会接二连三地组织大屠杀，这是顺理成章的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's very clear they are committed to this idea about driving the Jews out of Germany.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很显然，他们执着于把犹太人赶出德国这个想法。

sentences.en: I said there were many terrible things.
sentences.zh: 我刚才说有很多可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Another terrible thing, on the 10th of November, just a day or so later, the Nazis meet to decide who's going to pay for all this.
sentences.zh: 另一件可怕的事是，在11月10日，仅仅过了一天左右，纳粹开会决定谁来为这一切买单。

sentences.en: And they decide, well, the Jews will pay for it.
sentences.zh: 他们决定，好吧，由犹太人来买单。

sentences.en: They'll pay for it themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己出钱。

sentences.en: So on the 12th, Goering announces the economic measures that will be promulgated against the Jews.
sentences.zh: 因此在12日，戈林宣布了针对犹太人将要颁布的经济措施。

sentences.en: He says they will pay a fine for the damage that was inflicted upon them of one billion Reichsmarks.
sentences.zh: 他说，他们将为加诸自身的破坏支付10亿帝国马克的罚款。

sentences.en: Every Jewish family will have to hand over a quarter of their assets in order to pay for the damage.
sentences.zh: 每个犹太家庭都必须交出四分之一的财产来支付这笔破坏赔偿金。

sentences.en: There is a law on the exclusion of Jews from German economic life.
sentences.zh: 有一项关于将犹太人排除出德国经济生活的法律。

sentences.en: So you can't basically hold any meaningful occupation anymore if you're Jewish in Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是德国的犹太人，你基本上无法再从事任何有意义的职业了。

sentences.en: All remaining Jewish businesses, there aren't many left, but they will be
sentences.zh: 所有剩下的犹太人企业——虽然已经没剩多少了——但它们将被

sentences.en: Aryanized.
sentences.zh: “雅利安化”。

sentences.en: You know, they will be taken over by non-Jews.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们将被非犹太人接管。

sentences.en: They will basically be completely segregated now.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们基本上将被彻底隔离。

sentences.en: This is terrible in Victor Klemperer's diaries, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 维克托·克伦佩勒的日记里写得很糟糕，对吧？

sentences.en: He finds himself excluded from everything.
sentences.zh: 他发现自己被排斥在一切之外。

sentences.en: It's terrible.
sentences.zh: 太惨了。

sentences.en: Everything.
sentences.zh: 一切。

sentences.en: Can't go to the cinema.
sentences.zh: 不能去电影院。

sentences.en: Can't go to the theater.
sentences.zh: 不能去剧院。

sentences.en: Can't go to a concert.
sentences.zh: 不能去听音乐会。

sentences.en: Can't go to a swimming pool.
sentences.zh: 不能去游泳池。

sentences.en: A town now has the right to ban you from certain streets, from some parts of the town.
sentences.zh: 现在一个城镇有权禁止你进入某些街道、城镇的一些区域。

sentences.en: You cannot drive.
sentences.zh: 你不能开车。

sentences.en: You cannot go to a park.
sentences.zh: 你不能去公园。

sentences.en: You cannot go to a sports facility.
sentences.zh: 你不能去体育设施。

sentences.en: You cannot go to any swimming pool.
sentences.zh: 你不能去任何游泳池。

sentences.en: Heydrich suggests at this point that they should wear badges, yellow badges.
sentences.zh: 海德里希此时建议他们应该佩戴徽章，即黄色的徽章。

sentences.en: But that is not fully introduced, actually, until the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 但实际上直到第二次世界大战，这一政策才被全面推行。

sentences.en: But in a sense, it's irrelevant because at this point the Jews have been driven into virtual ghetto, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说这并不重要，因为我认为在这个时候，犹太人已经被逼入了实质上的隔都。

sentences.en: But also a bureaucratic ghetto.
sentences.zh: 但也是一个官僚化的隔都。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because their names are on public record.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的名字都记录在公共档案中。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: I mean, they've got the J stamps in their passport.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们的护照上盖了“J”字印章。

sentences.en: They've been renamed, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他们被重新起了名字，汤姆。

sentences.en: So some people do get out, 80,000 people or so.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有些人逃了出去，大约8万人左右。

sentences.en: They go to USA.
sentences.zh: 他们去了美国。

sentences.en: Some go to Britain.
sentences.zh: 有些人去了英国。

sentences.en: Some go to Holland until the Dutch close their borders.
sentences.zh: 有些人去了荷兰，直到荷兰关闭边境。

sentences.en: Some go to Brazil or
sentences.zh: 有些人去了巴西或

sentences.en: Argentina or Shanghai, actually.
sentences.zh: 阿根廷，或者实际上是上海。

sentences.en: A disproportionately high number, given its size.
sentences.zh: 考虑到上海的规模，其接收的人数比例高得离谱。

sentences.en: Go to the free port of
sentences.zh: 前往自由港

sentences.en: Shanghai, which has some of the laxist or most welcoming, shall we say, rules anywhere in the world about the admission of Jews.
sentences.zh: 上海，可以说，那里拥有世界上关于接纳犹太人最宽松、最欢迎的规定之一。

sentences.en: Britain doesn't.
sentences.zh: 英国则不然。

sentences.en: Britain really puts up the barrier.
sentences.zh: 英国真的竖起了高墙。

sentences.en: But having said that, is this when the kindertransport happens?
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，儿童难民营（Kindertransport）就是在这个时候发生的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: 10,000 or so Jewish children come to Britain.
sentences.zh: 大约有1万名犹太儿童来到英国。

sentences.en: But yes, no European state says, oh, you can all come here.
sentences.zh: 但没错，没有哪个欧洲国家会说，哦，你们都可以来这里。

sentences.en: Actually, most European neighbours are more anxious to try and keep out flows of refugees.
sentences.zh: 实际上，大多数欧洲邻国更加急于把难民潮挡在门外。

sentences.en: So about 80,000 people have left.
sentences.zh: 所以大约有8万人离开了。

sentences.en: But from the Nazi point of view, that is not enough.
sentences.zh: 但在纳粹看来，这还远远不够。

sentences.en: They have played their card, this huge pogrom, and there are still tens and tens of thousands of Jewish people left in Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们已经打出了这张牌，发动了这场巨大的大屠杀，而德国境内仍然残留着成千上万的犹太人。

sentences.en: So the question now is, what will they do?
sentences.zh: 所以现在的问题是，他们会怎么做？

sentences.en: And a couple of months later, the beginning of 1939, there is set up under Reinhard Heydrich, a central office for Jewish immigration.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，即1939年初，在雷因哈德·海德里希的领导下，成立了犹太人移民中央办公室。

sentences.en: This is the office that has been given the responsibility of, in inverted commas, removing the remaining Jewish population of Germany from the
sentences.zh: 这个办公室被赋予了这样的职责：用引号来说，就是将德国境内残存的犹太人口从

sentences.en: Reich and implicitly from Europe.
sentences.zh: 帝国清除出去，含蓄地说，也就是从欧洲清除出去。

sentences.en: And as Ian Kershaw says, this is a decisive step on the way that was to end in the gas chambers of the extermination camps.
sentences.zh: 正如伊恩·克肖所说，这是通往以灭绝营毒气室告终的那条道路上的决定性一步。

sentences.en: Because it is this commission, it is this post that Heydrich invokes when he opens the Vons A conference in January 1942.
sentences.zh: 因为正是这个委员会、正是这个职务，成了海德里希在1942年1月召开万湖会议时所引用的身份。

sentences.en: He says, I was given this job at the beginning of 1939 to get rid of the remaining Jews.
sentences.zh: 他说，我在1939年初被委任了这项工作，以清除剩下的犹太人。

sentences.en: And this is now what we're about to do.
sentences.zh: 而这就是我们现在要做的事。

sentences.en: So this is the bureaucratization and the industrialization of genocide.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是种族灭绝的官僚化和工业化。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: And I think Kristallnacht, for the reputation of Germany in the world, to anybody who had deluded themselves about the Nazi regime and its intentions, by the end of 1938,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为“水晶之夜”事件，对于德国在世界的声誉而言，对于任何曾经对纳粹政权及其意图抱有幻想的人来说，到1938年底时，

sentences.en: it is absolutely clear.
sentences.zh: 一切都绝对清晰明了了。

sentences.en: I mean, that editorial in the Yorkshire Post, I found online a selection, a sort of digest of British newspaper editorials reacting to this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如《约克郡邮报》的那篇社论，我在网上找到了一组精选集，算是对英国报纸社论对此反应的摘要。

sentences.en: And across the political spectrum, you know, so you've got on the right, the Telegraph, the Express, the Mail, and on the left,
sentences.zh: 跨越政治光谱，你知道的，右翼的有《电讯报》、《快报》、《邮报》，左翼的有

sentences.en: you have the kind of Manchester Guardian or whatever.
sentences.zh: 《曼彻斯特卫报》之类。

sentences.en: Across the political spectrum, the utter revulsion at Kristallnacht and what it represents.
sentences.zh: 整个政治光谱上下，对“水晶之夜”及其代表的一切都感到无比的厌恶。

sentences.en: You know, it's very profound.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是非常深刻的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: No one can argue about this anymore.
sentences.zh: 对此再也没有人可以争辩了。

sentences.en: Which in turn, Dominic, must mean that in the democracies, the hopes that appeasement will keep war at bay are starting to go into abeyance and retreat.
sentences.zh: 反过来，多米尼克，这一定意味着在民主国家中，妄想通过绥靖政策将战争阻挡在外的希望开始搁置并退潮。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为是这样。

sentences.en: And in Germany, therefore, when their ambassadors report this, their certainty that war is coming goes up even further.
sentences.zh: 因此在德国，当他们的外交官汇报这一情况时，他们对战争即将爆发的笃定更进了一步。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对如此。

sentences.en: And the implications of that for German Jews, again, is only bad.
sentences.zh: 这对德国犹太人意味着什么，同样，也只有坏结果。

sentences.en: Terrifying.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: Because the closer war comes, the more urgent the Nazi sense that they have to be eliminated.
sentences.zh: 因为战争越是逼近，纳粹那种必须将他们消灭的紧迫感就越是强烈。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Because one thing we haven't mentioned, of course, is that this happens in the aftermath of Munich.
sentences.zh: 因为我们还没有提到的一点是，这当然发生在慕尼黑事件之后。

sentences.en: So Hitler has taken the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia.
sentences.zh: 所以希特勒从捷克斯洛伐克夺取了苏台德地区。

sentences.en: It is clear that he is not going to moderate his ambitions.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，他并不打算收敛自己的野心。

sentences.en: You know, the world has come very close to war now in the autumn of 1938.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在1938年秋天，世界现在已经非常接近战争了。

sentences.en: People were relieved in Britain and France when that was averted by the appeasement of Munich.
sentences.zh: 当慕尼黑的绥靖政策避免了战争时，英国和法国的人民都松了一口气。

sentences.en: But I think a lot of people now think a reckoning is coming.
sentences.zh: 但我认为现在很多人认为清算即将来临。

sentences.en: And Hitler certainly thinks that a reckoning is coming.
sentences.zh: 而且希特勒也坚信清算即将来临。

sentences.en: I think what you get from Ian Kershaw's biography is a sense that in his own mind at the end of 1938, those two things that have
sentences.zh: 我认为从伊恩·克肖的传记中，你可以感受到在1938年底他的脑海中，有两件事情一直交织在一起，

sentences.en: always been interfused, which is the question of the Jewish population in Germany and his thirst
sentences.zh: 一个是关于德国犹太人口的问题，另一个是他对欧洲一场末日决战的渴望，

sentences.en: for an apocalyptic showdown in Europe, that those two things now loom larger than ever before.
sentences.zh: 这两件事现在比以往任何时候都更加重大。

sentences.en: There is even a kind of darker tinge to that, which is that even as Hitler is looking forward to war,
sentences.zh: 这其中甚至还有一种更黑暗的意味，那就是即使希特勒在期待战争、

sentences.en: planning for war, bringing war about, he is still kind of blaming it on the Jews, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 筹备战争、挑起战争，他却仍然把责任归咎于犹太人，不是吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: That it is the Jews who will be responsible if war breaks out, even as he is ordering his troops to prepare for invasions.
sentences.zh: 哪怕他在下令部队准备入侵时，他也认为如果爆发战争，犹太人将负有责任。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In his own mind, I guess, everything that he's doing is reactive.
sentences.zh: 我想在他的内心深处，他所做的一切都是被动反应。

sentences.en: All his preparations for war have been provoked and partly provoked by what happened in 1918.
sentences.zh: 他所有的战争准备都是被激怒的，部分是被1918年发生的事情所激怒。

sentences.en: So in January 1939, he has a meeting with the Czechoslovakian foreign minister.
sentences.zh: 所以在1939年1月，他与捷克斯洛伐克外长会面。

sentences.en: He says to him, if there is a war, the Jews here will be annihilated.
sentences.zh: 他对他说，如果有战争，这里的犹太人将被消灭。

sentences.en: The Jews didn't bring about the
sentences.zh: 犹太人没有白白引发

sentences.en: 9th of November 1918 for nothing.
sentences.zh: 1918年11月9日的那场事件。

sentences.en: This day will be avenged.
sentences.zh: 这一天将会被复仇。

sentences.en: And there's this sort of sense, I think, as we enter 1939, that Hitler now feels that the moment of vengeance is almost upon him.
sentences.zh: 我认为，当我们进入1939年时，有一种感觉，即希特勒现在觉得复仇的时刻几乎已经来临。

sentences.en: Vengeance against the French and the allies and the Poles and all of these people, but also vengeance on what he sees as the enemy within.
sentences.zh: 对法国人、盟友、波兰人以及所有这些人的复仇，同时也是对在他看来内部敌人的复仇。

sentences.en: We'll just end with this.
sentences.zh: 我们就以此结束吧。

sentences.en: On 30th of January 1939, it's the sixth anniversary of the moment he became Reich Chancellor.
sentences.zh: 1939年1月30日，是他成为帝国总理六周年的纪念日。

sentences.en: So the sixth anniversary of the kind of Nazis new order in Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是纳粹德国新秩序建立六周年的纪念日。

sentences.en: And he gives a speech to the Reichstag to mark it.
sentences.zh: 为此他在帝国议会发表了一场演讲。

sentences.en: And this speech is covered in full by the newsreels.
sentences.zh: 而这篇演讲被新闻短片全程报道了。

sentences.en: And he makes this horrendous prediction.
sentences.zh: 他做出了这个可怕的预言。

sentences.en: He says, I have very often in my lifetime been a prophet and I was derided.
sentences.zh: 他说，我一生中曾多次成为先知，而我却遭到嘲弄。

sentences.en: He says, you know, back in the old days, I used to prophesy that I would take over the leadership of Germany and I would deal with the Jewish problem.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，在过去的日子里，我曾预言我会接管德国的领导权，并且我会处理犹太人问题。

sentences.en: And the Jews used to laugh at me and they're not laughing anymore.
sentences.zh: 而犹太人过去常常嘲笑我，但他们现在再也笑不出来了。

sentences.en: And he says, I want today to be a prophet again.
sentences.zh: 他说，我今天想再次成为一个先知。

sentences.en: If international finance jury inside and outside Europe should succeed in plunging the nations once again into a world war.
sentences.zh: 如果欧洲境内外的国际犹太金融集团再次成功地将各国卷入世界大战。

sentences.en: See, again, as you say, Tom, he's blaming them.
sentences.zh: 看，汤姆，正如你所说，他又在指责他们了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's blaming the Jews.
sentences.zh: 是的，把责任推卸给犹太人。

sentences.en: The result will not be the Bolshevization of the earth and thereby the victory of jury.
sentences.zh: 其结果将不是地球的布尔什维克化，从而也不是犹太集团的胜利。

sentences.en: He says the result will be the annihilation of the Jewish race in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他说结果将是欧洲犹太民族的消灭。

sentences.en: And Tom, as everybody listened to this podcast will know, he had every intention of delivering on that prophecy.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，正如所有收听这个播客的人所知，他完全有决心兑现这个预言。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: That brings this episode and the series to a close.
sentences.zh: 这为主办的这一集和整个系列画上了句号。

sentences.en: Terrible, terrible story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其悲惨的故事。

sentences.en: And there is much more, of course, still to be told.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有更多的事情有待讲述。

sentences.en: The onset of war in Europe, the course of the war, the final destruction of Nazi Germany.
sentences.zh: 欧洲战争的爆发，战争的进程，纳粹德国的最终覆灭。

sentences.en: But that is all to come.
sentences.zh: 但这些都还在后面。

sentences.en: For now, we enjoyed the series.
sentences.zh: 就目前而言，我们很享受这个系列。

sentences.en: Maybe not the right word, but thank you for listening to it.
sentences.zh: 也许这个词用得不太对，但谢谢你们收听。

sentences.en: And Dominic, I guess we'll be picking up this story again, hopefully next January.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我想我们希望能在明年一月再次重拾这个故事。

sentences.en: But until then, and until the next shows, which will be next week, and hopefully on a slightly jollier theme, we'll see you.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，直到下周的新节目（希望是一个稍微欢快一点的主题），我们再见。

sentences.en: Bye bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
